title: Proverbs 30:26
text: The conies are only a feeble people, but they make their houses in the rocks;

title: Proverbs 30:27
text: The locusts have no king, but they all go out in bands;

title: Proverbs 30:28
text: You may take the lizard in your hands, but it is in kings' houses.

title: Proverbs 30:29
text: ¶There are three things whose steps are good to see, even four whose goings are fair:

title: Proverbs 30:30
text: The lion, which is strongest among beasts, not turning from his way for any;

title: Proverbs 30:31
text: The war-horse, and the he-goat, and the king when his army is with him.

title: Proverbs 30:32
text: If you have done foolishly in lifting yourself up, or if you have had evil designs, put your hand over your mouth.

title: Proverbs 30:33
text: The shaking of milk makes butter, and the twisting of the nose makes blood come: so the forcing of wrath is a cause of fighting.

title: Proverbs 31:1
text: ¶The words of Lemuel, king of Massa: the teaching which he had from his mother.

title: Proverbs 31:2
text: What am I to say to you, O Lemuel, my oldest son? and what, O son of my body? and what, O son of my oaths?

title: Proverbs 31:3
text: Do not give your strength to women, or your ways to that which is the destruction of kings.

title: Proverbs 31:4
text: It is not for kings, O Lemuel, it is not for kings to take wine, or for rulers to say, Where is strong drink?

title: Proverbs 31:5
text: For fear that through drinking they may come to have no respect for the law, wrongly judging the cause of those who are in trouble.

title: Proverbs 31:6
text: Give strong drink to him who is near to destruction, and wine to him whose soul is bitter:

title: Proverbs 31:7
text: Let him have drink, and his need will go from his mind, and the memory of his trouble will be gone.

title: Proverbs 31:8
text: Let your mouth be open for those who have no voice, in the cause of those who are ready for death.

title: Proverbs 31:9
text: Let your mouth be open, judging rightly, and give right decisions in the cause of the poor and those in need.

title: Proverbs 31:10
text: ¶Who may make discovery of a woman of virtue? For her price is much higher than jewels.

title: Proverbs 31:11
text: The heart of her husband has faith in her, and he will have profit in full measure.

title: Proverbs 31:12
text: She does him good and not evil all the days of her life.

title: Proverbs 31:13
text: She gets wool and linen, working at the business of her hands.

title: Proverbs 31:14
text: She is like the trading-ships, getting food from far away.

title: Proverbs 31:15
text: She gets up while it is still night, and gives meat to her family, and their food to her servant-girls.

title: Proverbs 31:16
text: After looking at a field with care, she gets it for a price, planting a vine-garden with the profit of her work.

title: Proverbs 31:17
text: She puts a band of strength round her, and makes her arms strong.

title: Proverbs 31:18
text: She sees that her marketing is of profit to her: her light does not go out by night.

title: Proverbs 31:19
text: She puts her hands to the cloth-working rod, and her fingers take the wheel.

title: Proverbs 31:20
text: Her hands are stretched out to the poor; yes, she is open-handed to those who are in need.

title: Proverbs 31:21
text: She has no fear of the snow for her family, for all those in her house are clothed in red.

title: Proverbs 31:22
text: She makes for herself cushions of needlework; her clothing is fair linen and purple.

title: Proverbs 31:23
text: Her husband is a man of note in the public place, when he takes his seat among the responsible men of the land.

title: Proverbs 31:24
text: She makes linen robes and gets a price for them, and traders take her cloth bands for a price.

title: Proverbs 31:25
text: Strength and self-respect are her clothing; she is facing the future with a smile.

title: Proverbs 31:26
text: Her mouth is open to give out wisdom, and the law of mercy is on her tongue.

title: Proverbs 31:27
text: She gives attention to the ways of her family, she does not take her food without working for it.

title: Proverbs 31:28
text: Her children get up and give her honour, and her husband gives her praise, saying,

title: Proverbs 31:29
text: Unnumbered women have done well, but you are better than all of them.

title: Proverbs 31:30
text: Fair looks are a deceit, and a beautiful form is of no value; but a woman who has the fear of the Lord is to be praised.

title: Proverbs 31:31
text: Give her credit for what her hands have made: let her be praised by her works in the public place.

title: Ecclesiastes 1:1
text: ¶The words of the Preacher, the son of David, king in Jerusalem.

title: Ecclesiastes 1:2
text: All is to no purpose, said the Preacher, all the ways of man are to no purpose.

title: Ecclesiastes 1:3
text: What is a man profited by all his work which he does under the sun?

title: Ecclesiastes 1:4
text: ¶One generation goes and another comes; but the earth is for ever.

title: Ecclesiastes 1:5
text: The sun comes up and the sun goes down, and goes quickly back to the place where he came up.

title: Ecclesiastes 1:6
text: The wind goes to the south, turning back again to the north; circling round for ever.

title: Ecclesiastes 1:7
text: All the rivers go down to the sea, but the sea is not full; to the place where the rivers go, there they go again.

title: Ecclesiastes 1:8
text: All things are full of weariness; man may not give their story: the eye has never enough of its seeing, or the ear of its hearing.

title: Ecclesiastes 1:9
text: ¶That which has been, is that which is to be, and that which has been done, is that which will be done, and there is no new thing under the sun.

title: Ecclesiastes 1:10
text: Is there anything of which men say, See, this is new? It has been in the old time which was before us.

title: Ecclesiastes 1:11
text: There is no memory of those who have gone before, and of those who come after there will be no memory for those who are still to come after them.

title: Ecclesiastes 1:12
text: ¶I, the Preacher, was king over Israel in Jerusalem.

title: Ecclesiastes 1:13
text: And I gave my heart to searching out in wisdom all things which are done under heaven: it is a hard thing which God has put on the sons of men to do.

title: Ecclesiastes 1:14
text: I have seen all the works which are done under the sun; all is to no purpose, and desire for wind.

title: Ecclesiastes 1:15
text: That which is bent may not be made straight, and that which is not there may not be numbered.

title: Ecclesiastes 1:16
text: I said to my heart, See, I have become great and am increased in wisdom more than any who were before me in Jerusalem--yes, my heart has seen much wisdom and knowledge.

title: Ecclesiastes 1:17
text: And I gave my heart to getting knowledge of wisdom, and of the ways of the foolish. And I saw that this again was desire for wind.

title: Ecclesiastes 1:18
text: Because in much wisdom is much grief, and increase of knowledge is increase of sorrow.

title: Ecclesiastes 2:1
text: ¶I said in my heart, I will give you joy for a test; so take your pleasure--but it was to no purpose.

title: Ecclesiastes 2:2
text: Of laughing I said, It is foolish; and of joy--What use is it?

title: Ecclesiastes 2:3
text: I made a search with my heart to give pleasure to my flesh with wine, still guiding my heart with wisdom, and to go after foolish things, so that I might see what was good for the sons of men to do under the heavens all the days of their life.

title: Ecclesiastes 2:4
text: I undertook great works, building myself houses and planting vine-gardens.

title: Ecclesiastes 2:5
text: I made myself gardens and fruit gardens, planting in them fruit-trees of all sorts.

title: Ecclesiastes 2:6
text: I made pools to give water for the woods with their young trees.

title: Ecclesiastes 2:7
text: I got men-servants and women-servants, and they gave birth to sons and daughters in my house. I had great wealth of herds and flocks, more than all who were in Jerusalem before me.

title: Ecclesiastes 2:8
text: I got together silver and gold and the wealth of kings and of countries. I got makers of song, male and female; and the delights of the sons of men--girls of all sorts to be my brides.

title: Ecclesiastes 2:9
text: And I became great; increasing more than all who had been before me in Jerusalem, and my wisdom was still with me.

title: Ecclesiastes 2:10
text: And nothing which was desired by my eyes did I keep from them; I did not keep any joy from my heart, because my heart took pleasure in all my work, and this was my reward.

title: Ecclesiastes 2:11
text: Then I saw all the works which my hands had made, and everything I had been working to do; and I saw that all was to no purpose and desire for wind, and there was no profit under the sun.

title: Ecclesiastes 2:12
text: ¶And I went again in search of wisdom and of foolish ways. What may the man do who comes after the king? The thing which he has done before.

title: Ecclesiastes 2:13
text: Then I saw that wisdom is better than foolish ways--as the light is better than the dark.

title: Ecclesiastes 2:14
text: The wise man's eyes are in his head, but the foolish man goes walking in the dark; but still I saw that the same event comes to them all.

title: Ecclesiastes 2:15
text: Then said I in my heart: As it comes to the foolish man, so will it come to me; so why have I been wise overmuch? Then I said in my heart: This again is to no purpose.

title: Ecclesiastes 2:16
text: Of the wise man, as of the foolish man, there is no memory for ever, seeing that those who now are will have gone from memory in the days to come. See how death comes to the wise as to the foolish!

title: Ecclesiastes 2:17
text: ¶So I was hating life, because everything under the sun was evil to me: all is to no purpose and desire for wind.

title: Ecclesiastes 2:18
text: Hate had I for all my work which I had done, because the man who comes after me will have its fruits.

title: Ecclesiastes 2:19
text: And who is to say if that man will be wise or foolish? But he will have power over all my work which I have done and in which I have been wise under the sun. This again is to no purpose.

title: Ecclesiastes 2:20
text: So my mind was turned to grief for all the trouble I had taken and all my wisdom under the sun.

title: Ecclesiastes 2:21
text: Because there is a man whose work has been done with wisdom, with knowledge, and with an expert hand; but one who has done nothing for it will have it for his heritage. This again is to no purpose and a great evil.

title: Ecclesiastes 2:22
text: What does a man get for all his work, and for the weight of care with which he has done his work under the sun?

title: Ecclesiastes 2:23
text: All his days are sorrow, and his work is full of grief. Even in the night his heart has no rest. This again is to no purpose.

title: Ecclesiastes 2:24
text: There is nothing better for a man than taking meat and drink, and having delight in his work. This again I saw was from the hand of God.

title: Ecclesiastes 2:25
text: Who may take food or have pleasure without him?

title: Ecclesiastes 2:26
text: To the man with whom he is pleased, God gives wisdom and knowledge and joy; but to the sinner he gives the work of getting goods together and storing up wealth, to give to him in whom God has pleasure. This again is to no purpose and desire for wind.

title: Ecclesiastes 3:1
text: ¶For everything there is a fixed time, and a time for every business under the sun.

title: Ecclesiastes 3:2
text: A time for birth and a time for death; a time for planting and a time for uprooting;

title: Ecclesiastes 3:3
text: A time to put to death and a time to make well; a time for pulling down and a time for building up;

title: Ecclesiastes 3:4
text: A time for weeping and a time for laughing; a time for sorrow and a time for dancing;

title: Ecclesiastes 3:5
text: A time to take stones away and a time to get stones together; a time for kissing and a time to keep from kissing;

title: Ecclesiastes 3:6
text: A time for search and a time for loss; a time to keep and a time to give away;

title: Ecclesiastes 3:7
text: A time for undoing and a time for stitching; a time for keeping quiet and a time for talk;

title: Ecclesiastes 3:8
text: A time for love and a time for hate; a time for war and a time for peace.

title: Ecclesiastes 3:9
text: What profit has the worker in the work which he does?

title: Ecclesiastes 3:10
text: I saw the work which God has put on the sons of man.

title: Ecclesiastes 3:11
text: ¶He has made everything right in its time; but he has made their hearts without knowledge, so that man is unable to see the works of God, from the first to the last.

title: Ecclesiastes 3:12
text: I am certain that there is nothing better for a man than to be glad, and to do good while life is in him.

title: Ecclesiastes 3:13
text: And for every man to take food and drink, and have joy in all his work, is a reward from God.

title: Ecclesiastes 3:14
text: I am certain that whatever God does will be for ever. No addition may be made to it, nothing may be taken from it; and God has done it so that man may be in fear before him.

title: Ecclesiastes 3:15
text: Whatever is has been before, and what is to be is now; because God makes search for the things which are past.

title: Ecclesiastes 3:16
text: ¶And again, I saw under the sun, in the place of the judges, that evil was there; and in the place of righteousness, that evil was there.

title: Ecclesiastes 3:17
text: I said in my heart, God will be judge of the good and of the bad; because a time for every purpose and for every work has been fixed by him.

title: Ecclesiastes 3:18
text: I said in my heart, It is because of the sons of men, so that God may put them to the test and that they may see themselves as beasts.

title: Ecclesiastes 3:19
text: Because the fate of the sons of men and the fate of the beasts is the same. As is the death of one so is the death of the other, and all have one spirit. Man is not higher than the beasts; because all is to no purpose.

title: Ecclesiastes 3:20
text: All go to one place, all are of the dust, and all will be turned to dust again.

title: Ecclesiastes 3:21
text: Who is certain that the spirit of the sons of men goes up to heaven, or that the spirit of the beasts goes down to the earth?

title: Ecclesiastes 3:22
text: So I saw that there is nothing better than for a man to have joy in his work--because that is his reward. Who will make him see what will come after him?

title: Ecclesiastes 4:1
text: ¶And again I saw all the cruel things which are done under the sun; there was the weeping of those who have evil done to them, and they had no comforter: and from the hands of the evil-doers there went out power, but they had no comforter.

title: Ecclesiastes 4:2
text: So my praise was for the dead who have gone to their death, more than for the living who still have life.

title: Ecclesiastes 4:3
text: Yes, happier than the dead or the living seemed he who has not ever been, who has not seen the evil which is done under the sun.

title: Ecclesiastes 4:4
text: ¶And I saw that the cause of all the work and of everything which is done well was man's envy of his neighbour. This again is to no purpose and a desire for wind.

title: Ecclesiastes 4:5
text: The foolish man, folding his hands, takes the flesh of his body for food.

title: Ecclesiastes 4:6
text: One hand full of rest is better than two hands full of trouble and desire for wind.

title: Ecclesiastes 4:7
text: ¶Then I came back, and I saw an example of what is to no purpose under the sun.

title: Ecclesiastes 4:8
text: It is one who is by himself, without a second, and without son or brother; but there is no end to all his work, and he has never enough of wealth. For whom, then, am I working and keeping myself from pleasure? This again is to no purpose, and a bitter work.

title: Ecclesiastes 4:9
text: Two are better than one, because they have a good reward for their work.

title: Ecclesiastes 4:10
text: And if one has a fall, the other will give him a hand; but unhappy is the man who is by himself, because he has no helper.

title: Ecclesiastes 4:11
text: So again, if two are sleeping together they are warm, but how may one be warm by himself?

title: Ecclesiastes 4:12
text: And two attacked by one would be safe, and three cords twisted together are not quickly broken.

title: Ecclesiastes 4:13
text: ¶A young man who is poor and wise is better than a king who is old and foolish and will not be guided by the wisdom of others.

title: Ecclesiastes 4:14
text: Because out of a prison the young man comes to be king, though by birth he was only a poor man in the kingdom.

title: Ecclesiastes 4:15
text: I saw all the living under the sun round the young man who was to be ruler in place of the king.

title: Ecclesiastes 4:16
text: There was no end of all the people, of all those whose head he was, but they who come later will have no delight in him. This again is to no purpose and desire for wind.

title: Ecclesiastes 5:1
text: ¶Put your feet down with care when you go to the house of God, for it is better to give ear than to make the burned offerings of the foolish, whose knowledge is only of doing evil.

title: Ecclesiastes 5:2
text: Be not unwise with your mouth, and let not your heart be quick to say anything before God, because God is in heaven and you are on the earth--so let not the number of your words be great.

title: Ecclesiastes 5:3
text: As a dream comes from much business, so the voice of a foolish man comes with words in great number.

title: Ecclesiastes 5:4
text: ¶When you take an oath before God, put it quickly into effect, because he has no pleasure in the foolish; keep the oath you have taken.

title: Ecclesiastes 5:5
text: It is better not to take an oath than to take an oath and not keep it.

title: Ecclesiastes 5:6
text: Let not your mouth make your flesh do evil. And say not before the angel, It was an error. So that God may not be angry with your words and put an end to the work of your hands.

title: Ecclesiastes 5:7
text: Because much talk comes from dreams and things of no purpose. But let the fear of God be in you.

title: Ecclesiastes 5:8
text: If you see the poor under a cruel yoke, and law and right being violently overturned in a country, be not surprised, because one authority is keeping watch on another and there are higher than they.

title: Ecclesiastes 5:9
text: ¶It is good generally for a country where the land is worked to have a king.

title: Ecclesiastes 5:10
text: He who has a love for silver never has enough silver, or he who has love for wealth, enough profit. This again is to no purpose.

title: Ecclesiastes 5:11
text: When goods are increased, the number of those who take of them is increased; and what profit has the owner but to see them?

title: Ecclesiastes 5:12
text: The sleep of a working man is sweet, if he has little food or much; but to him who is full, sleep will not come.

title: Ecclesiastes 5:13
text: There is a great evil which I have seen under the sun--wealth kept by the owner to be his downfall.

title: Ecclesiastes 5:14
text: And I saw the destruction of his wealth by an evil chance; and when he became the father of a son he had nothing in his hand.

title: Ecclesiastes 5:15
text: As he came from his mother at birth, so does he go again; he gets from his work no reward which he may take away in his hand.

title: Ecclesiastes 5:16
text: And this again is a great evil, that in all points as he came so will he go; and what profit has he in working for the wind?

title: Ecclesiastes 5:17
text: All his days are in the dark, and he has much sorrow, pain, disease, and trouble.

title: Ecclesiastes 5:18
text: ¶This is what I have seen: it is good and fair for a man to take meat and drink and to have joy in all his work under the sun, all the days of his life which God has given him; that is his reward.

title: Ecclesiastes 5:19
text: Every man to whom God has given money and wealth and the power to have pleasure in it and to do his part and have joy in his work: this is given by God.

title: Ecclesiastes 5:20
text: He will not give much thought to the days of his life; because God lets him be taken up with the joy of his heart.

title: Ecclesiastes 6:1
text: ¶There is an evil which I have seen under the sun, and it is hard on men;

title: Ecclesiastes 6:2
text: A man to whom God gives money, wealth, and honour so that he has all his desires but God does not give him the power to have joy of it, and a strange man takes it. This is to no purpose and an evil disease.

title: Ecclesiastes 6:3
text: If a man has a hundred children, and his life is long so that the days of his years are great in number, but his soul takes no pleasure in good, and he is not honoured at his death; I say that a birth before its time is better than he.

title: Ecclesiastes 6:4
text: In wind it came and to the dark it will go, and with the dark will its name be covered.

title: Ecclesiastes 6:5
text: Yes, it saw not the sun, and it had no knowledge; it is better with this than with the other.

title: Ecclesiastes 6:6
text: And though he goes on living a thousand years twice over and does not see good, are not the two going to the same place?

title: Ecclesiastes 6:7
text: ¶All the work of man is for his mouth, and still he has a desire for food.

title: Ecclesiastes 6:8
text: What have the wise more than the foolish? and what has the poor man by walking wisely before the living?

title: Ecclesiastes 6:9
text: What the eyes see is better than the wandering of desire. This is to no purpose and a desire for wind.

title: Ecclesiastes 6:10
text: That which is, has been named before, and of what man is there is knowledge. He has no power against one stronger than he.

title: Ecclesiastes 6:11
text: ¶There are words without number for increasing what is to no purpose, but what is man profited by them?

title: Ecclesiastes 6:12
text: Who is able to say what is good for man in life all the days of his foolish life which he goes through like a shade? who will say what is to be after him under the sun?

title: Ecclesiastes 7:1
text: ¶A good name is better than oil of great price, and the day of death than the day of birth.

title: Ecclesiastes 7:2
text: It is better to go to the house of weeping, than to go to the house of feasting; because that is the end of every man, and the living will take it to their hearts.

title: Ecclesiastes 7:3
text: Sorrow is better than joy; when the face is sad the mind gets better.

title: Ecclesiastes 7:4
text: The hearts of the wise are in the house of weeping; but the hearts of the foolish are in the house of joy.

title: Ecclesiastes 7:5
text: It is better to take note of the protest of the wise, than for a man to give ear to the song of the foolish.

title: Ecclesiastes 7:6
text: Like the cracking of thorns under a pot, so is the laugh of a foolish man; and this again is to no purpose.

title: Ecclesiastes 7:7
text: ¶The wise are troubled by the ways of the cruel, and the giving of money is the destruction of the heart.

title: Ecclesiastes 7:8
text: The end of a thing is better than its start, and a gentle spirit is better than pride.

title: Ecclesiastes 7:9
text: Be not quick to let your spirit be angry; because wrath is in the heart of the foolish.

title: Ecclesiastes 7:10
text: Say not, Why were the days which have gone by better than these? Such a question comes not from wisdom.

title: Ecclesiastes 7:11
text: ¶Wisdom together with a heritage is good, and a profit to those who see the sun.

title: Ecclesiastes 7:12
text: Wisdom keeps a man from danger even as money does; but the value of knowledge is that wisdom gives life to its owner.

title: Ecclesiastes 7:13
text: Give thought to the work of God. Who will make straight what he has made bent?

title: Ecclesiastes 7:14
text: In the day of wealth have joy, but in the day of evil take thought: God has put the one against the other, so that man may not be certain what will be after him.

title: Ecclesiastes 7:15
text: These two have I seen in my life which is to no purpose: a good man coming to his end in his righteousness, and an evil man whose days are long in his evil-doing.

title: Ecclesiastes 7:16
text: Be not given overmuch to righteousness and be not over-wise. Why let destruction come on you?

title: Ecclesiastes 7:17
text: Be not evil overmuch, and be not foolish. Why come to your end before your time?

title: Ecclesiastes 7:18
text: It is good to take this in your hand and not to keep your hand from that; he who has the fear of God will be free of the two.

title: Ecclesiastes 7:19
text: Wisdom makes a wise man stronger than ten rulers in a town.

title: Ecclesiastes 7:20
text: There is no man on earth of such righteousness that he does good and is free from sin all his days.

title: Ecclesiastes 7:21
text: Do not give ear to all the words which men say, for fear of hearing the curses of your servant.

title: Ecclesiastes 7:22
text: Your heart has knowledge how frequently others have been cursed by you.

title: Ecclesiastes 7:23
text: ¶All this I have put to the test by wisdom; I said, I will be wise, but it was far from me.

title: Ecclesiastes 7:24
text: Far off is true existence, and very deep; who may have knowledge of it?

title: Ecclesiastes 7:25
text: I gave my mind to knowledge and to searching for wisdom and the reason of things, and to the discovery that sin is foolish, and that to be foolish is to be without one's senses.

title: Ecclesiastes 7:26
text: And I saw a thing more bitter than death, even the woman whose heart is full of tricks and nets, and whose hands are as bands. He with whom God is pleased will get free from her, but the sinner will be taken by her.

title: Ecclesiastes 7:27
text: Look! this I have seen, said the Preacher, taking one thing after another to get the true account,

title: Ecclesiastes 7:28
text: For which my soul is still searching, but I have it not; one man among a thousand have I seen; but a woman among all these I have not seen.

title: Ecclesiastes 7:29
text: This only have I seen, that God made men upright, but they have been searching out all sorts of inventions.

title: Ecclesiastes 8:1
text: ¶Who is like the wise man? and to whom is the sense of anything clear? A man's wisdom makes his face shining, and his hard face will be changed.

title: Ecclesiastes 8:2
text: I say to you, Keep the king's law, from respect for the oath of God.

title: Ecclesiastes 8:3
text: Be not quick to go from before him. Be not fixed in an evil design, because he does whatever is pleasing to him.

title: Ecclesiastes 8:4
text: The word of a king has authority; and who may say to him, What is this you are doing?

title: Ecclesiastes 8:5
text: Whoever keeps the law will come to no evil: and a wise man's heart has knowledge of time and of decision.

title: Ecclesiastes 8:6
text: ¶For every purpose there is a time and a decision, because the sorrow of man is great in him.

title: Ecclesiastes 8:7
text: No one is certain what is to be, and who is able to say to him when it will be?

title: Ecclesiastes 8:8
text: No man has authority over the wind, to keep the wind; or is ruler over the day of his death. In war no man's time is free, and evil will not keep the sinner safe.

title: Ecclesiastes 8:9
text: ¶All this have I seen, and have given my heart to all the work which is done under the sun: there is a time when man has power over man for his destruction.

title: Ecclesiastes 8:10
text: And then I saw evil men put to rest, taken even from the holy place; and they went about and were praised in the town because of what they had done. This again is to no purpose.

title: Ecclesiastes 8:11
text: Because punishment for an evil work comes not quickly, the minds of the sons of men are fully given to doing evil.

title: Ecclesiastes 8:12
text: Though a sinner does evil a hundred times and his life is long, I am certain that it will be well for those who go in fear of God and are in fear before him.

title: Ecclesiastes 8:13
text: But it will not be well for the evil-doer; he will not make his days long like a shade, because he has no fear before God.

title: Ecclesiastes 8:14
text: ¶There is a thing which is to no purpose done on the earth: that there are good men to whom is given the same punishment as those who are evil, and there are evil men who get the reward of the good. I say that this again is to no purpose.

title: Ecclesiastes 8:15
text: So I gave praise to joy, because there is nothing better for a man to do under the sun than to take meat and drink and be happy; for that will be with him in his work all the days of his life which God gives him under the sun.

title: Ecclesiastes 8:16
text: When I gave my mind to the knowledge of wisdom and to seeing the business which is done on the earth (and there are those whose eyes see not sleep by day or by night),

title: Ecclesiastes 8:17
text: Then I saw all the work of God, and that man may not get knowledge of the work which is done under the sun; because, if a man gives hard work to the search he will not get knowledge, and even if the wise man seems to be coming to the end of his search, still he will be without knowledge.

title: Ecclesiastes 9:1
text: ¶All this I took to heart, and my heart saw it all: that the upright and the wise and their works are in the hand of God; and men may not be certain if it will be love or hate; all is to no purpose before them.

title: Ecclesiastes 9:2
text: Because to all there is one event, to the upright man and to the evil, to the clean and to the unclean, to him who makes an offering and to him who makes no offering; as is the good so is the sinner; he who takes an oath is as he who has fear of it.

title: Ecclesiastes 9:3
text: This is evil in all things which are done under the sun: that there is one fate for all, and the hearts of the sons of men are full of evil; while they have life their hearts are foolish, and after that--to the dead.

title: Ecclesiastes 9:4
text: ¶For him who is joined to all the living there is hope; a living dog is better than a dead lion.

title: Ecclesiastes 9:5
text: The living are conscious that death will come to them, but the dead are not conscious of anything, and they no longer have a reward, because there is no memory of them.

title: Ecclesiastes 9:6
text: Their love and their hate and their envy are now ended; and they have no longer a part for ever in anything which is done under the sun.

title: Ecclesiastes 9:7
text: Come, take your bread with joy, and your wine with a glad heart. God has taken pleasure in your works.

title: Ecclesiastes 9:8
text: Let your clothing be white at all times, and let not your head be without oil.

title: Ecclesiastes 9:9
text: Have joy with the woman of your love all the days of your foolish life which he gives you under the sun. Because that is your part in life and in your work which you do under the sun.

title: Ecclesiastes 9:10
text: Whatever comes to your hand to do with all your power, do it because there is no work, or thought, or knowledge, or wisdom in the place of the dead to which you are going.

title: Ecclesiastes 9:11
text: ¶And again I saw under the sun that the reward goes not to him who is quick, or the fruits of war to the strong; and there is no bread for the wise, or wealth for men of learning, or respect for those who have knowledge; but time and chance come to all.

title: Ecclesiastes 9:12
text: Even man has no knowledge of his time; like fishes taken in an evil net, or like birds taken by deceit, are the sons of men taken in an evil time when it comes suddenly on them.

title: Ecclesiastes 9:13
text: ¶This again I have seen under the sun as wisdom and it seemed great to me.

title: Ecclesiastes 9:14
text: There was a little town and the number of its men was small, and there came a great king against it and made an attack on it, building works of war round about it.

title: Ecclesiastes 9:15
text: Now there was in the town a poor, wise man, and he, by his wisdom, kept the town safe. But no one had any memory of that same poor man.

title: Ecclesiastes 9:16
text: Then I said, Wisdom is better than strength, but the poor man's wisdom is not respected, and his words are not given a hearing.

title: Ecclesiastes 9:17
text: The words of the wise which come quietly to the ear are noted more than the cry of a ruler among the foolish.

title: Ecclesiastes 9:18
text: Wisdom is better than instruments of war, but one sinner is the destruction of much good.

title: Ecclesiastes 10:1
text: ¶Dead flies make the oil of the perfumer give out an evil smell; more valued is a little wisdom than the great glory of the foolish.

title: Ecclesiastes 10:2
text: The heart of the wise man goes in the right direction; but the heart of a foolish man in the wrong.

title: Ecclesiastes 10:3
text: And when the foolish man is walking in the way, he has no sense and lets everyone see that he is foolish.

title: Ecclesiastes 10:4
text: ¶If the wrath of the ruler is against you, keep in your place; in him who keeps quiet even great sins may be overlooked.

title: Ecclesiastes 10:5
text: There is an evil which I have seen under the sun, like an error which comes by chance from a ruler:

title: Ecclesiastes 10:6
text: The foolish are placed in high positions, but men of wealth are kept low.

title: Ecclesiastes 10:7
text: I have seen servants on horses, and rulers walking on the earth as servants.

title: Ecclesiastes 10:8
text: He who makes a hole for others will himself go into it, and for him who makes a hole through a wall the bite of a snake will be a punishment.

title: Ecclesiastes 10:9
text: He who gets out stones from the earth will be damaged by them, and in the cutting of wood there is danger.

title: Ecclesiastes 10:10
text: If the iron has no edge, and he does not make it sharp, then he has to put out more strength; but wisdom makes things go well.

title: Ecclesiastes 10:11
text: If a snake gives a bite before the word of power is said, then there is no longer any use in the word of power.

title: Ecclesiastes 10:12
text: ¶The words of a wise man's mouth are sweet to all, but the lips of a foolish man are his destruction.

title: Ecclesiastes 10:13
text: The first words of his mouth are foolish, and the end of his talk is evil crime.

title: Ecclesiastes 10:14
text: The foolish are full of words; man has no knowledge of what will be; and who is able to say what will be after him?

title: Ecclesiastes 10:15
text: The work of the foolish will be a weariness to him, because he has no knowledge of the way to the town.

title: Ecclesiastes 10:16
text: ¶Unhappy is the land whose king is a boy, and whose rulers are feasting in the morning.

title: Ecclesiastes 10:17
text: Happy is the land whose ruler is of noble birth, and whose chiefs take food at the right time, for strength and not for feasting.

title: Ecclesiastes 10:18
text: When no work is done the roof goes in, and when the hands do nothing water comes into the house.

title: Ecclesiastes 10:19
text: A feast is for laughing, and wine makes glad the heart; but by the one and the other money is wasted.

title: Ecclesiastes 10:20
text: Say not a curse against the king, even in your thoughts; and even secretly say not a curse against the man of wealth; because a bird of the air will take the voice, and that which has wings will give news of it.

title: Ecclesiastes 11:1
text: ¶Put out your bread on the face of the waters; for after a long time it will come back to you again.

title: Ecclesiastes 11:2
text: Give a part to seven or even to eight, because you have no knowledge of the evil which will be on the earth.

title: Ecclesiastes 11:3
text: If the clouds are full of rain, they send it down on the earth; and if a tree comes down to the south, or the north, in whatever place it comes down, there it will be.

title: Ecclesiastes 11:4
text: He who is watching the wind will not get the seed planted, and he who is looking at the clouds will not get in the grain.

title: Ecclesiastes 11:5
text: As you have no knowledge of the way of the wind, or of the growth of the bones in the body of her who is with child, even so you have no knowledge of the works of God who has made all.

title: Ecclesiastes 11:6
text: In the morning put your seed into the earth, and till the evening let not your hand be at rest; because you are not certain which will do well, this or that--or if the two will be equally good.

title: Ecclesiastes 11:7
text: ¶Truly the light is sweet, and it is good for the eyes to see the sun.

title: Ecclesiastes 11:8
text: But even if a man's life is long and he has joy in all his years, let him keep in mind the dark days, because they will be great in number. Whatever may come is to no purpose.

title: Ecclesiastes 11:9
text: Have joy, O young man, while you are young; and let your heart be glad in the days of your strength, and go in the ways of your heart, and in the desire of your eyes; but be certain that for all these things God will be your judge.

title: Ecclesiastes 11:10
text: So put away trouble from your heart, and sorrow from your flesh; because the early years and the best years are to no purpose.

title: Ecclesiastes 12:1
text: ¶Let your mind be turned to your Maker in the days of your strength, while the evil days come not, and the years are far away when you will say, I have no pleasure in them;

title: Ecclesiastes 12:2
text: While the sun, or the light, or the moon, or the stars, are not dark, and the clouds come not back after the rain;

title: Ecclesiastes 12:3
text: In the day when the keepers of the house are shaking for fear, and the strong men are bent down, and the women who were crushing the grain are at rest because their number is small, and those looking out of the windows are unable to see;

title: Ecclesiastes 12:4
text: When the doors are shut in the street, and the sound of the crushing is low, and the voice of the bird is soft, and the daughters of music will be made low;

title: Ecclesiastes 12:5
text: And he is in fear of that which is high, and danger is in the road, and the tree is white with flower, and the least thing is a weight, and desire is at an end, because man goes to his last resting-place, and those who are sorrowing are in the streets;

title: Ecclesiastes 12:6
text: Before ever the silver cord is cut, or the vessel of gold is broken, or the pot is broken at the fountain, or the wheel broken at the water-hole;

title: Ecclesiastes 12:7
text: And the dust goes back to the earth as it was, and the spirit goes back to God who gave it.

title: Ecclesiastes 12:8
text: ¶All things are to no purpose, says the Preacher, all is to no purpose.

title: Ecclesiastes 12:9
text: And because the Preacher was wise he still gave the people knowledge; searching out, testing, and putting in order a great number of wise sayings.

title: Ecclesiastes 12:10
text: The Preacher made search for words which were pleasing, but his writing was in words upright and true.

title: Ecclesiastes 12:11
text: The words of the wise are pointed, and sayings grouped together are like nails fixed with a hammer; they are given by one guide.

title: Ecclesiastes 12:12
text: And further, my son, take note of this: of the making of books there is no end, and much learning is a weariness to the flesh.

title: Ecclesiastes 12:13
text: ¶This is the last word. All has been said. Have fear of God and keep his laws; because this is right for every man.

title: Ecclesiastes 12:14
text: God will be judge of every work, with every secret thing, good or evil.

title: Song of Solomon 1:1
text: ¶The song of Songs, which is Solomon's.

title: Song of Solomon 1:2
text: ¶Let him give me the kisses of his mouth: for his love is better than wine.

title: Song of Solomon 1:3
text: Sweet is the smell of your perfumes; your name is as perfume running out; so the young girls give you their love.

title: Song of Solomon 1:4
text: Take me to you, and we will go after you: the king has taken me into his house. We will be glad and full of joy in you, we will give more thought to your love than to wine: rightly are they your lovers.

title: Song of Solomon 1:5
text: I am dark, but fair of form, O daughters of Jerusalem, as the tents of Kedar, as the curtains of Solomon.

title: Song of Solomon 1:6
text: Let not your eyes be turned on me, because I am dark, because I was looked on by the sun; my mother's children were angry with me; they made me the keeper of the vine-gardens; but my vine-garden I have not kept.

title: Song of Solomon 1:7
text: ¶Say, O love of my soul, where you give food to your flock, and where you make them take their rest in the heat of the day; why have I to be as one wandering by the flocks of your friends?

title: Song of Solomon 1:8
text: If you have not knowledge, O most beautiful among women, go on your way in the footsteps of the flock, and give your young goats food by the tents of the keepers.

title: Song of Solomon 1:9
text: I have made a comparison of you, O my love, to a horse in Pharaoh's carriages.

title: Song of Solomon 1:10
text: Your face is a delight with rings of hair, your neck with chains of jewels.

title: Song of Solomon 1:11
text: We will make you chains of gold with ornaments of silver.

title: Song of Solomon 1:12
text: ¶While the king is seated at his table, my spices send out their perfume.

title: Song of Solomon 1:13
text: As a bag of myrrh is my well-loved one to me, when he is at rest all night between my breasts.

title: Song of Solomon 1:14
text: My love is to me as a branch of the cypress-tree in the vine-gardens of En-gedi.

title: Song of Solomon 1:15
text: See, you are fair, my love, you are fair; you have the eyes of a dove.

title: Song of Solomon 1:16
text: See, you are fair, my loved one, and a pleasure; our bed is green.

title: Song of Solomon 1:17
text: Cedar-trees are the pillars of our house; and our boards are made of fir-trees.

title: Song of Solomon 2:1
text: ¶I am a rose of Sharon, a flower of the valleys.

title: Song of Solomon 2:2
text: As the lily-flower among the thorns of the waste, so is my love among the daughters.

title: Song of Solomon 2:3
text: ¶As the apple-tree among the trees of the wood, so is my loved one among the sons. I took my rest under his shade with great delight, and his fruit was sweet to my taste.

title: Song of Solomon 2:4
text: He took me to the house of wine, and his flag over me was love.

title: Song of Solomon 2:5
text: Make me strong with wine-cakes, let me be comforted with apples; I am overcome with love.

title: Song of Solomon 2:6
text: His left hand is under my head, and his right hand is round about me.

title: Song of Solomon 2:7
text: I say to you, O daughters of Jerusalem, by the roes of the field, do not let love be moved till it is ready.

title: Song of Solomon 2:8
text: ¶The voice of my loved one! See, he comes dancing on the mountains, stepping quickly on the hills.

title: Song of Solomon 2:9
text: My loved one is like a roe; see, he is on the other side of our wall, he is looking in at the windows, letting himself be seen through the spaces.

title: Song of Solomon 2:10
text: My loved one said to me, Get up, my love, my fair one, and come away.

title: Song of Solomon 2:11
text: For, see, the winter is past, the rain is over and gone;

title: Song of Solomon 2:12
text: The flowers are come on the earth; the time of cutting the vines is come, and the voice of the dove is sounding in our land;

title: Song of Solomon 2:13
text: The fig-tree puts out her green fruit and the vines with their young fruit give a good smell. Get up from your bed, my beautiful one, and come away.

title: Song of Solomon 2:14
text: ¶O my dove, you are in the holes of the mountain sides, in the cracks of the high hills; let me see your face, let your voice come to my ears; for sweet is your voice, and your face is fair.

title: Song of Solomon 2:15
text: Take for us the foxes, the little foxes, which do damage to the vines; our vines have young grapes.

title: Song of Solomon 2:16
text: My loved one is mine, and I am his: he takes his food among the flowers.

title: Song of Solomon 2:17
text: Till the evening comes, and the sky slowly becomes dark, come, my loved one, and be like a roe on the mountains of Bether.

title: Song of Solomon 3:1
text: ¶By night on my bed I was looking for him who is the love of my soul: I was looking for him, but I did not see him.

title: Song of Solomon 3:2
text: I will get up now and go about the town, in the streets and in the wide ways I will go after him who is the love of my soul: I went after him, but I did not see him.

title: Song of Solomon 3:3
text: The watchmen who go about the town came by me; to them I said, Have you seen him who is my heart's desire?

title: Song of Solomon 3:4
text: I was but a little way from them, when I came face to face with him who is the love of my soul. I took him by the hands, and did not let him go, till I had taken him into my mother's house, and into the room of her who gave me birth.

title: Song of Solomon 3:5
text: I say to you, O daughters of Jerusalem, by the roes of the field, let not love be moved till it is ready.

title: Song of Solomon 3:6
text: ¶Who is this coming out of the waste places like pillars of smoke, perfumed with sweet spices, with all the spices of the trader?

title: Song of Solomon 3:7
text: ¶See, it is the bed of Solomon; sixty men of war are about it, of the army of Israel,

title: Song of Solomon 3:8
text: All of them armed with swords, trained in war; every man has his sword at his side, because of fear in the night.

title: Song of Solomon 3:9
text: King Solomon made himself a bed of the wood of Lebanon.

title: Song of Solomon 3:10
text: He made its pillars of silver, its base of gold, its seat of purple, the middle of it of ebony.

title: Song of Solomon 3:11
text: Go out, O daughters of Jerusalem, and see King Solomon, with the crown which his mother put on his head on the day when he was married, and on the day of the joy of his heart.

title: Song of Solomon 4:1
text: ¶See, you are fair, my love, you are fair; you have the eyes of a dove; your hair is as a flock of goats, which take their rest on the side of Gilead.

title: Song of Solomon 4:2
text: Your teeth are like a flock of sheep whose wool is newly cut, which come up from the washing; every one has two lambs, and there is not one without young.

title: Song of Solomon 4:3
text: Your red lips are like a bright thread, and your mouth is fair of form; the sides of your head are like pomegranate fruit under your veil.

title: Song of Solomon 4:4
text: Your neck is like the tower of David made for a store-house of arms, in which a thousand breastplates are hanging, breastplates for fighting-men.

title: Song of Solomon 4:5
text: Your two breasts are like two young roes of the same birth, which take their food among the lilies.

title: Song of Solomon 4:6
text: Till the evening comes, and the sky slowly becomes dark, I will go to the mountain of myrrh, and to the hill of frankincense.

title: Song of Solomon 4:7
text: You are all fair, my love; there is no mark on you.

title: Song of Solomon 4:8
text: ¶Come with me from Lebanon, my bride, with me from Lebanon; see from the top of Amana, from the top of Senir and Hermon, from the places of the lions, from the mountains of the leopards.

title: Song of Solomon 4:9
text: You have taken away my heart, my sister, my bride; you have taken away my heart, with one look you have taken it, with one chain of your neck!

title: Song of Solomon 4:10
text: How fair is your love, my sister! How much better is your love than wine, and the smell of your oils than any perfume!

title: Song of Solomon 4:11
text: Your lips are dropping honey; honey and milk are under your tongue; and the smell of your clothing is like the smell of Lebanon.

title: Song of Solomon 4:12
text: A garden walled-in is my sister, my bride; a garden shut up, a spring of water stopped.

title: Song of Solomon 4:13
text: The produce of the garden is pomegranates; with all the best fruits, henna and spikenard,

title: Song of Solomon 4:14
text: Spikenard and safron; calamus and cinnamon, with all trees of frankincense; myrrh and aloes, with all the chief spices.

title: Song of Solomon 4:15
text: ¶You are a fountain of gardens, a spring of living waters, and flowing waters from Lebanon.

title: Song of Solomon 4:16
text: Be awake, O north wind; and come, O south, blowing on my garden, so that its spices may come out. Let my loved one come into his garden, and take of his good fruits.

title: Song of Solomon 5:1
text: ¶I have come into my garden, my sister, my bride; to take my myrrh with my spice; my wax with my honey; my wine with my milk. Take meat, O friends; take wine, yes, be overcome with love.

title: Song of Solomon 5:2
text: ¶I am sleeping, but my heart is awake; it is the sound of my loved one at the door, saying, Be open to me, my sister, my love, my dove, my very beautiful one; my head is wet with dew, and my hair with the drops of the night.

title: Song of Solomon 5:3
text: I have put off my coat; how may I put it on? My feet are washed; how may I make them unclean?

title: Song of Solomon 5:4
text: My loved one put his hand on the door, and my heart was moved for him.

title: Song of Solomon 5:5
text: I got up to let my loved one in; and my hands were dropping with myrrh, and my fingers with liquid myrrh, on the lock of the door.

title: Song of Solomon 5:6
text: I made the door open to my loved one; but my loved one had taken himself away, and was gone, my soul was feeble when his back was turned on me; I went after him, but I did not come near him; I said his name, but he gave me no answer.

title: Song of Solomon 5:7
text: The keepers who go about the town overtook me; they gave me blows and wounds; the keepers of the walls took away my veil from me.

title: Song of Solomon 5:8
text: I say to you, O daughters of Jerusalem, if you see my loved one, what will you say to him? That I am overcome with love.

title: Song of Solomon 5:9
text: ¶What is your loved one more than another, O fairest among women? What is your loved one more than another, that you say this to us?

title: Song of Solomon 5:10
text: My loved one is white and red, the chief among ten thousand.

title: Song of Solomon 5:11
text: His head is as the most delicate gold; his hair is thick, and black as a raven.

title: Song of Solomon 5:12
text: His eyes are as the eyes of doves by the water streams, washed with milk, and rightly placed.

title: Song of Solomon 5:13
text: His face is as beds of spices, giving out perfumes of every sort; his lips like lilies, dropping liquid myrrh.

title: Song of Solomon 5:14
text: His hands are as rings of gold ornamented with beryl-stones; his body is as a smooth plate of ivory covered with sapphires.

title: Song of Solomon 5:15
text: His legs are as pillars of stone on a base of delicate gold; his looks are as Lebanon, beautiful as the cedar-tree.

title: Song of Solomon 5:16
text: His mouth is most sweet; yes, he is all beautiful. This is my loved one, and this is my friend, O daughters of Jerusalem.

title: Song of Solomon 6:1
text: ¶Where is your loved one gone, O most fair among women? Where is your loved one turned away, that we may go looking for him with you?

title: Song of Solomon 6:2
text: My loved one is gone down into his garden, to the beds of spices, to take food in the gardens, and to get lilies.

title: Song of Solomon 6:3
text: I am for my loved one, and my loved one is for me; he takes food among the lilies.

title: Song of Solomon 6:4
text: ¶You are beautiful, O my love, as Tirzah, as fair as Jerusalem; you are to be feared like an army with flags.

title: Song of Solomon 6:5
text: Let your eyes be turned away from me; see, they have overcome me; your hair is as a flock of goats which take their rest on the side of Gilead.

title: Song of Solomon 6:6
text: Your teeth are like a flock of sheep which come up from the washing; every one has two lambs, and there is not one without young.

title: Song of Solomon 6:7
text: Like pomegranate fruit are the sides of your head under your veil.

title: Song of Solomon 6:8
text: There are sixty queens, and eighty servant-wives, and young girls without number.

title: Song of Solomon 6:9
text: My dove, my very beautiful one, is but one; she is the only one of her mother, she is the dearest one of her who gave her birth. The daughters saw her, and gave her a blessing; yes, the queens and the servant-wives, and they gave her praises.

title: Song of Solomon 6:10
text: Who is she, looking down as the morning light, fair as the moon, clear as the sun, who is to be feared like an army with flags?

title: Song of Solomon 6:11
text: ¶I went down into the garden of nuts to see the green plants of the valley, and to see if the vine was in bud, and the pomegranate-trees were in flower.

title: Song of Solomon 6:12
text: Before I was conscious of it, ...

title: Song of Solomon 6:13
text: Come back, come back, O Shulammite; come back, come back, so that our eyes may see you. What will you see in the Shulammite? A sword-dance.

title: Song of Solomon 7:1
text: ¶How beautiful are your feet in their shoes, O king's daughter! The curves of your legs are like jewels, the work of the hands of a good workman:

title: Song of Solomon 7:2
text: Your stomach is a store of grain with lilies round it, and in the middle a round cup full of wine.

title: Song of Solomon 7:3
text: Your two breasts are like two young roes of the same birth.

title: Song of Solomon 7:4
text: Your neck is as a tower of ivory; your eyes like the waters in Heshbon, by the doorway of Bath-rabbim; your nose is as the tower on Lebanon looking over Damascus:

title: Song of Solomon 7:5
text: Your head is like Carmel, and the hair of your head is like purple, in whose net the king is prisoner.

title: Song of Solomon 7:6
text: How beautiful and how sweet you are, O love, for delight.

title: Song of Solomon 7:7
text: You are tall like a palm-tree, and your breasts are like the fruit of the vine.

title: Song of Solomon 7:8
text: I said, Let me go up the palm-tree, and let me take its branches in my hands: your breasts will be as the fruit of the vine, and the smell of your breath like apples;

title: Song of Solomon 7:9
text: And the roof of your mouth like good wine flowing down smoothly for my loved one, moving gently over my lips and my teeth.

title: Song of Solomon 7:10
text: ¶I am for my loved one, and his desire is for me.

title: Song of Solomon 7:11
text: Come, my loved one, let us go out into the field; let us take rest among the cypress-trees.

title: Song of Solomon 7:12
text: Let us go out early to the vine-gardens; let us see if the vine is in bud, if it has put out its young fruit, and the pomegranate is in flower. There I will give you my love.

title: Song of Solomon 7:13
text: The mandrakes give out a sweet smell, and at our doors are all sorts of good fruits, new and old, which I have kept for my loved one.

title: Song of Solomon 8:1
text: ¶Oh that you were my brother, who took milk from my mother's breasts! When I came to you in the street, I would give you kisses; yes, I would not be looked down on.

title: Song of Solomon 8:2
text: I would take you by the hand into my mother's house, and she would be my teacher. I would give you drink of spiced wine, drink of the pomegranate.

title: Song of Solomon 8:3
text: His left hand would be under my head, and his right hand about me.

title: Song of Solomon 8:4
text: I say to you, O daughters of Jerusalem, do not let love be moved till it is ready.

title: Song of Solomon 8:5
text: ¶Who is this, who comes up from the waste places, resting on her loved one? It was I who made you awake under the apple-tree, where your mother gave you birth; there she was in pain at your birth.

title: Song of Solomon 8:6
text: Put me as a sign on your heart, as a sign on your arm; love is strong as death, and wrath bitter as the underworld: its coals are coals of fire; violent are its flames.

title: Song of Solomon 8:7
text: Much water may not put out love, or the deep waters overcome it: if a man would give all the substance of his house for love, it would be judged a price not great enough.

title: Song of Solomon 8:8
text: ¶We have a young sister, and she has no breasts; what are we to do for our sister in the day when she is given to a man?

title: Song of Solomon 8:9
text: If she is a wall, we will make on her a strong base of silver; and if she is a door, we will let her be shut up with cedar-wood.

title: Song of Solomon 8:10
text: I am a wall, and my breasts are like towers; then was I in his eyes as one to whom good chance had come.

title: Song of Solomon 8:11
text: Solomon had a vine-garden at Baal-hamon; he let out the vine-garden to keepers; every one had to give a thousand bits of silver for its fruit.

title: Song of Solomon 8:12
text: My vine-garden, which is mine, is before me: you, O Solomon, will have the thousand, and those who keep the fruit of them two hundred.

title: Song of Solomon 8:13
text: ¶You who have your resting-place in the gardens, the friends give ear to your voice; make me give ear to it.

title: Song of Solomon 8:14
text: Come quickly, my loved one, and be like a roe on the mountains of spice.

title: Isaiah 1:1
text: ¶The vision of Isaiah, the son of Amoz, which he saw about Judah and Jerusalem, in the days of Uzziah, Jotham, Ahaz, and Hezekiah, kings of Judah.

title: Isaiah 1:2
text: ¶Give ear, O heavens, and you, O earth, to the word which the Lord has said: I have taken care of my children till they became men, but their hearts have been turned away from me.

title: Isaiah 1:3
text: Even the ox has knowledge of its owner, and the ass of the place where its master puts its food: but Israel has no knowledge, my people give no thought to me.

title: Isaiah 1:4
text: O nation full of sin, a people weighted down with crime, a generation of evil-doers, false-hearted children: they have gone away from the Lord, they have no respect for the Holy One of Israel, their hearts are turned back from him.

title: Isaiah 1:5
text: Why will you have more and more punishment? why keep on in your evil ways? Every head is tired and every heart is feeble.

title: Isaiah 1:6
text: The body, from head to foot, is all diseased; it is a mass of open wounds, marks of blows, and broken flesh: the flow of blood has not been stopped, and no oil has been put on the wounds.

title: Isaiah 1:7
text: Your country has become waste; your towns are burned with fire; as for your land, it is overturned before your eyes, made waste and overcome by men from strange lands.

title: Isaiah 1:8
text: And the daughter of Zion has become like a tent in a vine-garden, like a watchman's house in a field of fruit, like a town shut in by armies.

title: Isaiah 1:9
text: If the Lord of armies had not kept some at least of us safe, we would have been like Sodom, and the fate of Gomorrah would have been ours.

title: Isaiah 1:10
text: ¶Give ear to the word of the Lord, you rulers of Sodom; let your hearts be turned to the law of our God, you people of Gomorrah.

title: Isaiah 1:11
text: What use to me is the number of the offerings which you give me? says the Lord; your burned offerings of sheep, and the best parts of fat cattle, are a weariness to me; I take no pleasure in the blood of oxen, or of lambs, or of he-goats.

title: Isaiah 1:12
text: At whose request do you come before me, making my house unclean with your feet?

title: Isaiah 1:13
text: Give me no more false offerings; the smoke of burning flesh is disgusting to me, so are your new moons and Sabbaths and your holy meetings.

title: Isaiah 1:14
text: Your new moons and your regular feasts are a grief to my soul: they are a weight in my spirit; I am crushed under them.

title: Isaiah 1:15
text: And when your hands are stretched out to me, my eyes will be turned away from you: even though you go on making prayers, I will not give ear: your hands are full of blood.

title: Isaiah 1:16
text: ¶Be washed, make yourselves clean; put away the evil of your doings from before my eyes; let there be an end of sinning;

title: Isaiah 1:17
text: Take pleasure in well-doing; let your ways be upright, keep down the cruel, give a right decision for the child who has no father, see to the cause of the widow.

title: Isaiah 1:18
text: Come now, and let us have an argument together, says the Lord: how may your sins which are red like blood be white as snow? how may their dark purple seem like wool?

title: Isaiah 1:19
text: If you will give ear to my word and do it, the good things of the land will be yours;

title: Isaiah 1:20
text: But if your hearts are turned against me, I will send destruction on you by the sword; so the Lord has said.

title: Isaiah 1:21
text: ¶The upright town has become untrue; there was a time when her judges gave right decisions, when righteousness had a resting-place in her, but now she is full of those who take men's lives.

title: Isaiah 1:22
text: Your silver is no longer true metal, your wine is mixed with water.

title: Isaiah 1:23
text: Your chiefs have gone against the Lord, they have become friends of thieves; every one of them is looking for profit and going after rewards; they do not give right decisions for the child who has no father, and they do not let the cause of the widow come before them.

title: Isaiah 1:24
text: For this reason the Lord, the Lord of armies, the Strong One of Israel, has said, I will put an end to my haters, and send punishment on those who are against me;

title: Isaiah 1:25
text: And my hand will again be on you, washing away what is unclean as with soap, and taking away all your false metal;

title: Isaiah 1:26
text: And I will give you judges again as at the first, and wise guides as in the past; then you will be named, The Town of Righteousness, the true town.

title: Isaiah 1:27
text: Upright acts will be the price of Zion's forgiveness, and by righteousness will men be living there.

title: Isaiah 1:28
text: But a common destruction will overtake sinners and evil-doers together, and those who have gone away from the Lord will be cut off.

title: Isaiah 1:29
text: For you will be put to shame because of the trees of your desire, and because of the gardens of your pleasure.

title: Isaiah 1:30
text: For you will be like a tree whose leaves have become dry, and like a garden without water.

title: Isaiah 1:31
text: And the strong will be as food for the fire, and his work as a flame; and they will be burned together, with no one to put out the fire.

title: Isaiah 2:1
text: ¶The word which Isaiah, the son of Amoz, saw about Judah and Jerusalem.

title: Isaiah 2:2
text: And it will come about in the last days, that the mountain of the Lord will be placed on the top of the mountains, and be lifted up over the hills; and all nations will come to it.

title: Isaiah 2:3
text: And the peoples will say, Come, and let us go up to the mountain of the Lord, to the house of the God of Jacob: and he will give us knowledge of his ways, and we will be guided by his word; for out of Zion the law will go out, and the word of the Lord from Jerusalem.

title: Isaiah 2:4
text: And he will be the judge between the nations, and the peoples will be ruled by his decisions: and their swords will be turned into plough-blades, and their spears into vine-knives: no longer will the nations be turning their swords against one another, and the knowledge of war will be gone for ever.

title: Isaiah 2:5
text: O family of Jacob, come, and let us go in the light of the Lord.

title: Isaiah 2:6
text: ¶For you, O Lord, have given up your people, the family of Jacob, because they are full of the evil ways of the east, and make use of secret arts like the Philistines, and are friends with the children of strange countries.

title: Isaiah 2:7
text: And their land is full of silver and gold, and there is no end to their stores; their land is full of horses, and there is no end to their carriages.

title: Isaiah 2:8
text: Their land is full of images; they give worship to the work of their hands, even to that which their fingers have made.

title: Isaiah 2:9
text: And the poor man's head is bent, and the great man goes down on his face: for this cause there will be no forgiveness for their sin.

title: Isaiah 2:10
text: ¶Go into a hole in the rock, covering yourselves with dust, in fear of the Lord, before the glory of his power.

title: Isaiah 2:11
text: The high looks of man will be put to shame, and the pride of men will be made low, and only the Lord will be lifted up in that day.

title: Isaiah 2:12
text: For the day of the Lord of armies is coming on all the pride of men, and on all who are high and lifted up;

title: Isaiah 2:13
text: And on all the high trees of Lebanon, and on all the strong trees of Bashan;

title: Isaiah 2:14
text: And on all the high mountains, and on all the hills which are lifted up;

title: Isaiah 2:15
text: And on every high tower, and on every strong wall;

title: Isaiah 2:16
text: And on all the ships of Tarshish, and on all the fair boats.

title: Isaiah 2:17
text: And the high looks of man will be put to shame, and the pride of men will be made low: and only the Lord will be lifted up in that day.

title: Isaiah 2:18
text: And the images will never be seen again.

title: Isaiah 2:19
text: And men will go into cracks of the rocks, and into holes of the earth, for fear of the Lord, and before the glory of his power, when he comes out of his place, shaking the earth with his strength.

title: Isaiah 2:20
text: In that day men will put their images of silver and of gold, which they made for worship, in the keeping of the beasts of the dark places;

title: Isaiah 2:21
text: To take cover in the cracks of the rocks, and in the holes of the hills, for fear of the Lord, and before the glory of his power, when he comes out of his place, shaking the earth with his strength.

title: Isaiah 2:22
text: Have no more to do with man, whose life is only a breath, for he is of no value.

title: Isaiah 3:1
text: ¶For the Lord, the Lord of armies, is about to take away from Jerusalem and from Judah all their support; their store of bread and of water;

title: Isaiah 3:2
text: The strong man and the man of war; the judge and the prophet; the man who has knowledge of secret arts, and the man who is wise because of his years;

title: Isaiah 3:3
text: The captain of fifty, and the man of high position, and the wise guide, and the wonder-worker, and he who makes use of secret powers.

title: Isaiah 3:4
text: And I will make children their chiefs, and foolish ones will have rule over them.

title: Isaiah 3:5
text: And the people will be crushed, every one by his neighbour; the young will be full of pride against the old, and those of low position will be lifted up against the noble.

title: Isaiah 3:6
text: When one man puts his hand on another in his father's house, and says, You have clothing, be our ruler and be responsible for us in our sad condition:

title: Isaiah 3:7
text: Then he will say with an oath, I will not be a helper, for in my house there is no bread or clothing: I will not let you make me a ruler of the people.

title: Isaiah 3:8
text: For Jerusalem has become feeble, and destruction has come on Judah, because their words and their acts are against the Lord, moving the eyes of his glory to wrath.

title: Isaiah 3:9
text: ¶Their respect for a man's position is a witness against them; and their sin is open to the view of all; like that of Sodom, it is not covered. A curse on their soul! for the measure of their sin is full.

title: Isaiah 3:10
text: Happy is the upright man! for he will have joy of the fruit of his ways.

title: Isaiah 3:11
text: Unhappy is the sinner! for the reward of his evil doings will come on him.

title: Isaiah 3:12
text: As for my people, their ruler is acting like a child, and those who have authority over them are women. O my people, your guides are the cause of your wandering, turning your footsteps out of the right way.

title: Isaiah 3:13
text: The Lord is ready to take up his cause against his people, and is about to come forward as their judge.

title: Isaiah 3:14
text: The Lord comes to be the judge of their responsible men and of their rulers: it is you who have made waste the vine-garden, and in your houses is the property of the poor which you have taken by force.

title: Isaiah 3:15
text: By what right are you crushing my people, and putting a bitter yoke on the necks of the poor? This is the word of the Lord, the Lord of armies.

title: Isaiah 3:16
text: ¶Again, the Lord has said, Because the daughters of Zion are full of pride, and go with outstretched necks and wandering eyes, with their foot-chains sounding when they go:

title: Isaiah 3:17
text: The Lord will send disease on the heads of the daughters of Zion, and the Lord will let their secret parts be seen.

title: Isaiah 3:18
text: In that day the Lord will take away the glory of their foot-rings, and their sun-jewels, and their moon-ornaments,

title: Isaiah 3:19
text: The ear-rings, and the chains, and the delicate clothing,

title: Isaiah 3:20
text: The head-bands, and the arm-chains, and the worked bands, and the perfume-boxes, and the jewels with secret powers,

title: Isaiah 3:21
text: The rings, and the nose-jewels,

title: Isaiah 3:22
text: The feast-day dresses, and the robes, and the wide skirts, and the handbags,

title: Isaiah 3:23
text: The looking-glasses, and the fair linen, and the high head-dresses, and the veils.

title: Isaiah 3:24
text: And in the place of sweet spices will be an evil smell, and for a fair band a thick cord; for a well-dressed head there will be the cutting-off of the hair, and for a beautiful robe there will be the clothing of sorrow; the mark of the prisoner in place of the ornaments of the free.

title: Isaiah 3:25
text: Your men will be put to the sword, and your men of war will come to destruction in the fight.

title: Isaiah 3:26
text: And in the public places of her towns will be sorrow and weeping; and she will be seated on the earth, waste and uncovered.

title: Isaiah 4:1
text: ¶And in that day seven women will put their hands on one man, saying, There will be no need for you to give us food or clothing, only let us go under your name, so that our shame may be taken away.

title: Isaiah 4:2
text: ¶In that day will the young growth of the Lord be beautiful in glory, and the fruit of the earth will be the pride of those who are still living in Israel.

title: Isaiah 4:3
text: And it will come about that the rest of the living in Zion, and of those who have been kept from destruction in Jerusalem, will be named holy, even everyone who has been recorded for life in Jerusalem:

title: Isaiah 4:4
text: When Zion has been washed from her sin by the Lord, and Jerusalem made clean from her blood by a judging and a burning wind.

title: Isaiah 4:5
text: And over every living-place on Mount Zion, all over all her meetings, the Lord will make a cloud and smoke by day, and the shining of a flaming fire by night, for over all, the glory of the Lord will be a cover and a tent;

title: Isaiah 4:6
text: And a shade in the daytime from the heat, and a safe cover from storm and from rain.

title: Isaiah 5:1
text: ¶Let me make a song about my loved one, a song of love for his vine-garden. My loved one had a vine-garden on a fertile hill:

title: Isaiah 5:2
text: And after working the earth of it with a spade, he took away its stones, and put in it a very special vine; and he put up a watchtower in the middle of it, hollowing out in the rock a place for the grape-crushing; and he was hoping that it would give the best grapes, but it gave common grapes.

title: Isaiah 5:3
text: And now, you people of Jerusalem and you men of Judah, be the judges between me and my vine-garden.

title: Isaiah 5:4
text: Is there anything which might have been done for my vine-garden which I have not done? why then, when I was hoping for the best grapes did it give me common grapes?

title: Isaiah 5:5
text: And now, this is what I will do to my vine-garden: I will take away the circle of thorns round it, and it will be burned up; its wall will be broken down and the beasts of the field will go through it;

title: Isaiah 5:6
text: And I will make it waste; its branches will not be touched with the knife, or the earth worked with the spade; but blackberries and thorns will come up in it: and I will give orders to the clouds not to send rain on it.

title: Isaiah 5:7
text: For the vine-garden of the Lord of armies is the people of Israel, and the men of Judah are the plant of his delight: and he was looking for upright judging, and there was blood; for righteousness, and there was a cry for help.

title: Isaiah 5:8
text: ¶Cursed are those who are joining house to house, and putting field to field, till there is no more living-space for any but themselves in all the land!

title: Isaiah 5:9
text: The Lord of armies has said to me secretly, Truly, numbers of great and fair houses will be waste, with no one living in them.

title: Isaiah 5:10
text: For ten fields of vines will only give one measure of wine, and a great amount of seed will only give a small measure of grain.

title: Isaiah 5:11
text: Cursed are those who get up early in the morning to give themselves up to strong drink; who keep on drinking far into the night till they are heated with wine!

title: Isaiah 5:12
text: And corded instruments and wind-instruments and wine are in their feasts: but they give no thought to the work of the Lord, and they are not interested in what his hands are doing.

title: Isaiah 5:13
text: For this cause my people are taken away as prisoners into strange countries for need of knowledge: and their rulers are wasted for need of food, and their loud-voiced feasters are dry for need of water.

title: Isaiah 5:14
text: For this cause the underworld has made wide its throat, opening its mouth without limit: and her glory, and the noise of her masses, and her loud-voiced feasters, will go down into it.

title: Isaiah 5:15
text: And the poor man's head is bent, and the great man goes down on his face, and the eyes of pride are put to shame:

title: Isaiah 5:16
text: But the Lord of armies is lifted up as judge, and the Holy God is seen to be holy in righteousness.

title: Isaiah 5:17
text: Then the lambs will get food as in their grass-lands, and the fat cattle will be feasting in the waste places.

title: Isaiah 5:18
text: ¶Cursed are those who make use of ox-cords for pulling the evil thing, and the bands of a young ox for their sin!

title: Isaiah 5:19
text: Who say, Let him do his work quickly, let him make it sudden, so that we may see it: let the design of the Holy One of Israel come near, so that it may be clear to us.

title: Isaiah 5:20
text: Cursed are those who give the name of good to evil, and of evil to what is good: who make light dark, and dark light: who make bitter sweet, and sweet bitter!

title: Isaiah 5:21
text: Cursed are those who seem wise to themselves, and who take pride in their knowledge!

title: Isaiah 5:22
text: Cursed are those who are strong to take wine, and great in making mixed drinks!

title: Isaiah 5:23
text: Who for a reward give support to the cause of the sinner, and who take away the righteousness of the upright from him.

title: Isaiah 5:24
text: For this cause, as the waste of the grain is burned up by tongues of fire, and as the dry grass goes down before the flame, so their root will be like the dry stems of grain, and their flower will go up in dust: because they have gone against the law of the Lord of armies, and have given no honour to the word of the Holy One of Israel.

title: Isaiah 5:25
text: For this reason the wrath of the Lord has been burning against his people, and his hand has been stretched out against them in punishment, and the hills were shaking, and their dead bodies were like waste in the open places of the town.

title: Isaiah 5:26
text: And he will let a flag be lifted up as a sign to a far-off nation, whistling to them from the ends of the earth: and they will come quickly and suddenly.

title: Isaiah 5:27
text: There is no weariness among them, and no man is feeble-footed: they come without resting or sleeping, and the cord of their shoes is not broken.

title: Isaiah 5:28
text: Their arrows are sharp, and every bow is bent: the feet of their horses are like rock, and their wheels are like a rushing storm.

title: Isaiah 5:29
text: The sound of their armies will be like the voice of a lion, and their war-cry like the noise of young lions: with loud cries they will come down on their food and will take it away safely, and there will be no one to take it out of their hands.

title: Isaiah 5:30
text: And his voice will be loud over him in that day like the sounding of the sea: and if a man's eyes are turned to the earth, it is all dark and full of trouble; and the light is made dark by thick clouds.

title: Isaiah 6:1
text: ¶In the year of King Uzziah's death I saw the Lord seated in his place, high and lifted up, and the Temple was full of the wide skirts of his robe.

title: Isaiah 6:2
text: Over him were the winged ones: every one had six wings; two for covering his face, two for covering his feed, and two for flight.

title: Isaiah 6:3
text: And one said in a loud voice to another, Holy, holy, holy, is the Lord of armies: all the earth is full of his glory.

title: Isaiah 6:4
text: And the bases of the door-pillars were shaking at the sound of his cry, and the house was full of smoke.

title: Isaiah 6:5
text: ¶Then I said, The curse is on me, and my fate is destruction; for I am a man of unclean lips, living among a people of unclean lips; for my eyes have seen the King, the Lord of armies.

title: Isaiah 6:6
text: Then a winged one came to me with a burning coal in his hand, which he had taken from off the altar with the fire-spoon.

title: Isaiah 6:7
text: And after touching my mouth with it, he said, See, your lips have been touched with this; and your evil is taken away, and you are made clean from sin.

title: Isaiah 6:8
text: And the voice of the Lord came to my ears, saying, Whom am I to send, and who will go for us? Then I said, Here am I, send me.

title: Isaiah 6:9
text: ¶And he said, Go, and say to this people, You will go on hearing, but learning nothing; you will go on seeing, but without getting wiser.

title: Isaiah 6:10
text: Make the hearts of this people fat, and let their ears be stopped, and their eyes shut; for fear that they may see with their eyes, and be hearing with their ears, and their heart may become wise, and they may be turned to me and made well.

title: Isaiah 6:11
text: Then I said, Lord, how long? And he said in answer, Till the towns are waste and unpeopled, and the houses have no men, and the land becomes completely waste,

title: Isaiah 6:12
text: And the Lord has taken men far away, and there are wide waste places in the land.

title: Isaiah 6:13
text: And even if there is still a tenth part in it, it will again be burned, like a tree of the woods whose broken end is still in the earth after the tree has been cut down (the holy seed is the broken end).

title: Isaiah 7:1
text: ¶Now it came about in the days of Ahaz, the son of Jotham, the son of Uzziah, king of Judah, that Rezin, the king of Aram, and Pekah, the son of Remaliah, the king of Israel, came up to Jerusalem to make war against it, but were not able to overcome it.

title: Isaiah 7:2
